title: Sustainment Period - 2yr vs Job Creation
summary: NPRM proposes 2-year sustainment. Anonymous 0080 argues 2yr insufficient, cites Portugal ARI 5yr and Yellowstone same-project money-back obligation. Concern about at-risk requirement.

opinions.label: Tie to job creation not time
opinions.stance: Sustainment should end when jobs created and I-829 eligible, not arbitrary 2yr
fragments: Statutory requirement is job creation, not calendar
2yr clock starting at investment creates mismatch with construction timelines
At-risk must remain but job-based test is cleaner

opinions.label: 5yr benchmark like Portugal ARI
opinions.stance: 2yr too short for large projects, prefer 5yr or conditional extension
fragments: Large TEA rural projects have 3-4yr construction, 2yr forces premature redeployment
Portugal Golden Visa 5yr sustainment offers stability model
If 2yr retained, clarify start date = filing of I-526E or investment

opinions.label: 2yr workable if clarified
opinions.stance: 2yr is okay but need clarity on start, redeployment, money-back
fragments: Clarify 2yr starts at investment date not conditional GC
Money-back obligation for same project (Yellowstone) should not break sustainment
Allow redeployment within same NCE/JCE without new TEA determination

title: Bridge Financing 204.407(e)(1)
summary: Comment 0077 Intellex Capital attaches brief arguing bridge financing prohibition retroactively eliminates capital stacking used since 2013. Concern about retro cutoff.

opinions.label: Allow bridge in good faith
opinions.stance: Bridge used before EB-5 capital should not disqualify job creation
fragments: Bridge financing is standard market practice to start construction, EB-5 replaces bridge
Since 2013 industry relied on interim financing, sudden elimination harms reliance
Allow bridge if disclosed and EB-5 replaces within reasonable time

opinions.label: Limit but transition
opinions.stance: Prohibit future bridge but grandfather existing projects
fragments: Grandfather projects with I-956F filed before NPRM effective date
Require bridge be temporary less than 18 months

title: Grandfather Clause / Retroactivity
cfrs: INA 203(b)(5) as amended by RIA March 15 2022
summary: Should post-RIA sustainment / TEA rules apply to investors who filed I-526E after March 15 2022 but before effective date. Comment 0079 Ankit Dave argues retroactive expansion harms investors who relied on 800k TEA and filed I-526E in 2025.

opinions.label: No retroactive application
opinions.stance: Rules should apply only to petitions filed after final rule effective date, RIA March 15 2022 is statutory cutoff not regulatory cutoff
fragments: Applying new sustainment/bridge restrictions to cases that filed in reliance on existing RIA guidance violates reliance interests
Investors who filed I-526E at 800k TEA in 2025 made irreversible capital commitment
Grandfather under 204.400(a) should track RIA enactment March 15 2022 not future rulemaking effective date

opinions.label: Limited retroactivity with transition
opinions.stance: Allow pending cases 180-day grace or elect old rule
fragments: Transition period would reduce I-829 denials based on bridge financing elimination since 2013
USCIS should publish clear election for pending I-526E to opt into old 204.423(b)

opinions.label: Pro retro uniformity
opinions.stance: Program integrity requires same rule for all pending
fragments: Uniform application avoids two-track adjudication
Final rule should clarify prospective only to avoid litigation

title: TEA Designation & Deference
summary: Concern that TEA redesignation on redeployment or sustainment extension could cause TEA loss mid-process.

opinions.label: Lock TEA at filing
opinions.stance: TEA at time of I-526E filing should lock for sustainment and I-829
fragments: Investors cannot control census tract changes after locking capital
Deference policy should lock TEA at 90 days after filing

opinions.label: Allow State letter deference
opinions.stance: Give deference to state TEA letter at I-956F stage
fragments: State high-unemployment determinations should get deference, avoid USCIS recalculating

title: Program Integrity / redeployment / money-back
summary: Yellowstone same project money-back and redeployment flexibility argued in 0080. Investor worried 2yr plus at-risk plus money-back guarantee conflicts.

opinions.label: Allow same-project return obligation
opinions.stance: Money-back if jobs not created in same project should not violate at-risk
fragments: At-risk is about equity risk not guarantee of return, same-project obligation is normal
Prohibit only third-party guarantees, not developer refund if project fails

opinions.label: Strict at-risk
opinions.stance: Any return obligation violates at-risk, market needs discipline
fragments: RIA tightened at-risk to curb fraud, keep prohibition broad

title: Definitional Asymmetry 204.432 vs 204.433
summary: Comment 0076 points to asymmetry between regional center vs direct definitions of new commercial enterprise and job creating entity.

opinions.label: Harmonize definitions
opinions.stance: Same NCE/JCE definitions should apply to RC and direct
fragments: Current asymmetry creates disparate treatment of identical investments
Align 204.432 and 204.433 to reduce RFE risk

opinions.label: Keep distinction but clarify
opinions.stance: Distinction intentional, but clarify when each applies
fragments: RC vs direct serve different policy, need plain language guide with examples
